proposal.actor: government and legislature enacting the citizenship and marriage restrictions
proposal.action: Enact the proposed blood-based citizenship and intimate-relationship restrictions.
proposal.purpose: preserve the state's asserted racial and national order
proposal.requested_authority: Enact the proposed blood-based citizenship and intimate-relationship restrictions.

evidence.claim: The country's preceding constitutional tradition stated equality before law and rejected public-law privilege or disadvantage based on birth or rank.
The proposed citizenship law reserves full citizenship and political rights to people of an approved blood category who meet loyalty/fitness criteria.
The proposed second law prohibits marriage and sexual relations between the targeted minority and people of the approved blood category.
The proposed legal disadvantages attach to assigned group/blood status rather than requiring proof that a particular affected person committed a harmful or disloyal act.
The government argues that preserving the majority's blood and racial national community is essential to the nation's continued existence.
The legislation delegates important future definition and implementation questions to executive authorities.
The legislature is controlled by the governing movement and lacks ordinary plural opposition capable of independently checking the proposal.

No individualised evidential test is supplied connecting minority status, ancestry or a consensual intimate relationship to a concrete harmful act ordinarily relevant to loss of citizenship or civil rights.

affected_parties.party: Members of the targeted minority and people the state may assign to it
affected_parties.interests_or_risks: Citizenship, political rights, equality before law, marriage, intimate relationships, livelihood/status consequences and protection from arbitrary inherited classification.

affected_parties.party: People assigned to the favoured majority blood category
affected_parties.interests_or_risks: Freedom of relationships, civic identity and the consequences of state policing of ancestry and private life.

affected_parties.party: People of mixed or disputed ancestry
affected_parties.interests_or_risks: Uncertain legal status, family rights and exposure to future administrative classification.
Ability to define national membership and regulate civic/private life according to the governing ideology.
Rule-of-law precedent, social cohesion and future expansion of ancestry-based unequal legal status.

alternatives.description: Reject the group-based restrictions and retain equal citizenship/civil-law treatment.
Address genuine acts of violence, disloyalty, espionage or public danger through conduct-based law applying equally to individuals.
Use neutral citizenship criteria and independent legal process rather than inherited group identity.
Retain equal citizenship and political rights without ancestry-based exclusion.
Use ordinary criminal/security laws against individually evidenced harmful conduct rather than identity.
Leave marriage and consensual adult relationships governed by general civil law rather than blood classification.
Require any serious citizenship limitation to be based on individually reviewable conduct and independent legal process.

uncertainties: The exact ancestry/classification rules the executive will later use.
How broadly the blood-based citizenship principle will be extended to other rights, occupations or groups.
How aggressively police, courts and administrators will enforce the intimate-relationship prohibitions.
The long-term social and political effects of converting ideological group categories into legal status.
requested_capability: Enact the proposed blood-based citizenship and intimate-relationship restrictions.
